request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may carry tags on the person form (comma separated, trimmed, lower-cased, repeats dropped;
shown sorted, comma and space separated). The tag totals count a claim for a tag when the claim or
its person carries it, once.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now carry tags, and claims count in the tag totals under their person's tags as well as their own. `bin/e2e` builds the app and passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V64__person_tags.sql`, adds a `tags` column to `person`.
- **Server:** the person form tidies tags the same way claim tags already are — trimmed, lower-cased, blanks and repeats dropped, sorted (it reuses `ClaimForm.tags`). Adding or editing a person saves their tags. Those tags also go into the sheet's list of tags ever used, so a tag only a person carries still gets its own total. The audit lines for adding and editing a person are unchanged, as the test expects.
- **Front end:** the person form has a Tags field (`person-form-tags`). It is filled with the person's current tags when you open the editor, or when someone else saved them in the meantime. Each person row shows its tags (`person-tags`), separated by a comma and a space. In `TagTotals.tsx`, a claim counts for a tag if the claim or its person carries it, and only once when both do. Saving a person refreshes the tag list.

Importing people doesn't set tags: an import line has no tags field, so a person added by import starts with none. And because the tag list keeps every tag ever used, a tag removed from everyone stays in the totals at `0.00`, the same as claim tags do today.
